links.targetTitle: A Prime Agent may be its own Integrator and earn the Distrib

title: Reserved Reward Code ranges and published Integrator lists let Prime Agents onboard partners without a central bottleneck
content:
A.2.2.9.1.2.1.1.3 states the objective directly: Operational GovOps manages the list of Actor Reward Codes, and all current and onboarding Integrators must be specified in the Atlas "so that Prime Agents, through their Operational Executor Agents, can onboard new partners themselves **without having to go through a single party**."

Two mechanisms deliver it. First, namespace partitioning: A.2.2.9.1.2.1.1.4 allocates each named Prime Agent a reserved range of Reward Codes, so codes can be issued in parallel without collision or a central allocator serializing requests. Second, published registries: Current Integrators (A.2.2.9.1.2.1.4.1) and Onboarding Integrators (A.2.2.9.1.2.1.4.2) are maintained as Active Data under Operational GovOps with Direct Edit, giving every Agent a live, authoritative view of who is already in the program and at what stage.

The distinction between the two lists is functional rather than cosmetic. Current Integrators have a Reward Code in an `Active` Primitive Instance; Onboarding Integrators are approved but sit in a Pending or not-yet-Active Instance. An Agent can therefore see approved-but-unattached actors and pursue them, which is only possible because the intermediate state is published rather than held privately by the approver.

What is *not* decentralized is approval. Reward Codes are still assigned by Operational GovOps (A.2.2.9.1.2.1.1.1.1), which "may contract with another actor to perform this work." The pattern is consistent with the Integrator Program generally: distribute discovery and coordination, retain the gate.
description: Each Prime Agent gets its own code namespace and Operational GovOps maintains the current and onboarding Integrator lists as Active Data, so Agents can act without queueing behind one party.
